images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of Gamer.A generalist game agent framework operates across a broad range of visually and mechanically diverse games. At each step, the agent uses the current screen, task context, recent interaction history, long-term memory, and reasoning to generate native keyboard and mouse actions in real time. The agent interacts continuously through this loop. Cross-game training, multi-level supervision, and persistent memory support transferable control and sustained task execution.

Figure 2:CPT for unified keyboard-mouse control.Synchronized gameplay observations and device events are mapped to a shared action representation. Random key remapping reduces reliance on key identity, while repeat-aware loss decay reweights temporally persistent actions. The resulting control prior is used by the subsequent task-conditioned training stages.

header: 3Supervised Fine-Tuning for Sparse Reasoning and Cross-Context Memory

images.caption: Figure 4:Sparse reasoning and cross-context memory in supervised fine-tuning.The shared autoregressive policy integrates visual observations, task memory, optional reasoning, and executable keyboard-mouse actions. Context memory compaction preserves task progress across long interactions, while adaptive reasoning allows the policy to act directly at routine steps and generate explicit reasoning when needed.

Figure 5:Memory-linked long-horizon optimization with TA-GRPO. A long interaction may exceed the model’s context budget (top). Memory compaction divides online rollouts into finite segments whose task states remain connected by generated summaries (bottom). Segments at corresponding stages are compared using environment-verifiable outcomes, and temporal credit assignment distributes their group-relative advantage across decisions. The figure is schematic, and model execution uses the real-time serving backend in Sec.5.

Figure 6:Streaming-vLLM for persistent multi-environment inference.Each game client maintains separate short-term history, long-term memory, and logical KV-cache state. Paged allocation and memory-aware KV-cache reuse avoid repeated context processing, while incremental rotary position embedding (RoPE) refresh corrects retained keys after compaction. The runtime combines architecture-aware execution, BF16-verified FSM speculation, and early action dispatch to serve concurrent real-time interactions.

Figure 7:Bottom-up construction of multi-level task supervision.The diagram illustrates the organization of aligned gameplay segments into local operations, intermediate subgoals, and extended task stages. Separate GPT-5.6-Luna passes produce sparse Think annotations, segment-level instructions and scene descriptions, and memory updates as detailed in Secs.6.2-6.3. The diagram focuses on hierarchy assembly rather than depicting every annotation call.

Ferocity contains 55 milestones and additionally includes three mechanical-repair puzzles. Both panels show ordered milestone sequences and configured step budgets rather than measured completion times.

Figure 10:Overview of the minigame benchmark in the Honkai: Star Rail evaluation suite.The benchmark contains 40 task instances across seven game types. The left panel shows representative gameplay examples, instance counts, and mechanics. The upper-right chart shows the number of instances per type, while the lower-right chart groups minigames by four descriptive primary capability tags, with instance totals in parentheses. Each minigame type is assigned one primary tag for counting and may require additional abilities. Screenshots illustrate game types and are not necessarily drawn from the evaluated instances.
